headline.fallback: A customer story picked for {{ account.name }}

dek.fallback: One of our customers was in a similar spot to {{ account.name }}. Here is what they changed and what happened next.

fit.fallback: Every story we tell started with a team that looked a lot like {{ account.name }} from the outside. On a short call I can tell you which parts would carry over to you, and which would not.

recipe.prompt:
You are writing a customer story page for {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). {{ sender.name | default: 'The sender' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} sends it. The page retells one story about one of our customers, so that {{ account.name }} can see their own situation in it. "We" and "us" mean {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}.

Inputs: data.stories are our customer stories from the same industry as {{ account.name }}. data.size_matches are stories from companies the same size. Each row has customer, industry, size_band, problem, approach, result_metric, result_value, timeframe, quote and quote_author_title. What we know about {{ account.name }}: account.industry, account.size_band, account.dossier.summary and account.dossier.why_now. Nothing else.

Step 1, pick one story. Prefer data.stories, and among them the row whose size_band is {{ account.size_band }} and whose problem fits the dossier best. If data.stories is empty, pick the row in data.size_matches whose problem is closest to what a company in {{ account.industry }} deals with, judged from the dossier. If both lists are empty, return {} and nothing else.

Step 2, return JSON with these keys, all about that one story:
- headline: at most 90 characters. What the customer got, said so it speaks to {{ account.name }}, like "How a builder your size cut invoice approvals from 19 days to 4". Numbers come from result_value exactly as written.
- dek: 1 or 2 sentences, 40 to 240 characters, on why this story is worth two minutes of {{ account.name }}'s time.
- customer: the customer name, copied exactly.
- customer_about: who the customer is, at most 140 characters, from their industry and size_band only, like "A construction company with 51 to 200 people".
- parallel: 2 or 3 items {label, them, you} on what the customer and {{ account.name }} have in common. label is at most 28 characters. them is at most 200 characters, from the story row. you is at most 200 characters, from what we know about {{ account.name }}. Leave out any line where we know nothing about {{ account.name }}; never guess.
- before: 2 to 4 sentences, at most 600 characters, retelling the problem from the row.
- after: 2 to 4 sentences, at most 600 characters, retelling what they changed with us, from the approach column, and how it went.
- result: {metric, value, timeframe}, copied exactly from result_metric, result_value and timeframe.
- quote: {text, author_title}, copied word for word from quote and quote_author_title. Leave the key out if the row has no quote.
- fit: 2 to 4 sentences, 60 to 700 characters, on why this story applies to {{ account.name }}, plus one honest line on what is different for them.

Facts: use only what the chosen row and the inputs say. Never invent customers, people, names, numbers, tools or results, and never add a number that is not in the row. Do not name the person behind the quote; use the title only.

Voice: one person telling a peer about a customer. Plain, specific, a little warm. Short sentences a person would say out loud. Sentence case for the headline.

Rules for every string: no em dashes or en dashes. No email addresses or phone numbers. No hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, crucial, elevate, delve, transform, game changer). Never "real" as emphasis.
